Suzukawa"Then I must destroy it! With these hands only! Before the beasts feed on it! At least—while it is still beautiful!"

Suzukawa"My wife and daughter. Their beautiful faces weakening with sickness. Those mouths that always gave me such warm words, giving only gasps of pain. In front of my eyes. And I could do nothing."

Suzukawa"Hope, yaar! I could not let it go! Somewhere there is a saviour, mercy will come to us, somebody will save us—this HOPE!"

Suzukawa"Malice rules this age. Beautiful things will certainly be lost. Protecting them till the end is not possible. So..."
Suzukawa"All you beautiful things I love. These hands of mine will destroy you."

Except the SIZE. Kya mazaak hai?

Its head was above Suzukawa's. Half the body—more than half, maybe—was still under the floor. One leg, only one out of that whole crowd, was the size of a human arm.

A centipede like this existed? No. Nature had not made this arrangement. A normal centipede was already enough centipede. Nobody needed to stand beside one and feel insufficiently developed.

Look properly. That shell did not look like steel because of some resemblance. It WAS steel.

Tsurugi.

The history lecture I had listened to with half an ear came back. Now the other half was interested also. A high-grade tsurugi, forged by a master, could take an animal's form and move by itself.
